title: ess-history-adapter/1
description: How the lines of a recorded command/response log map onto ess-history/1 operations, as declared by models/recorded-log-adapter/ and read by `ess verify conform import-history`. Each source is the word absent or an object naming a JSON pointer into one log line; every source but rows must be declared.

Absent.description: The log does not carry this field.

Completion.description: concurrent.history.Completion, which the log's word for a completion means.

JsonPointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON pointer into one log line.

MappedCompletion.description: Where the completion is, and what each of the log's words for it means. A word not listed is refused on import.

values.description: Each of the log's words and the completion it means. A key here is a string word: it maps a log value that is that string, and the key "200" maps the string "200", not the number 200. A JSON object's keys are always strings, so this schema, which describes the JSON spelling, admits string words only. An adapter written in YAML may also use an integer key (200: Returned), which maps a log value that is that integer; that spelling has no JSON form. A word is mapped once: a YAML adapter mapping both 200 and "200" is refused.

rows.description: A JSON array of row identities, for a read of a view. Absent when left out.
